name: the rich tooltip shows on a tap again
why: Removes the touch guard from _initStatTooltip()'s mouseover: a tap's compatibility mouseover shows #mb-stat-tooltip and no mouseout ever hides it (org/mobile.org bug 1).

edits.find:
// A tap: no mouseout would ever hide it again.
            if (_isTouchCompatMouseEvent(e)) return;

name: the touch guard answers false for every event
why: Keeps every call site but makes the predicate inert, so a guard that is wired yet never true is caught too. The mouse-hover controls must still pass on their own; the tap assertions must fail.
grep: hover tooltips on a touch device

name: the art hover preview shows on a tap again
why: Removes the guard from _showArtHoverPreview() only. The per-image type tooltip keeps its own guard, so the spec must notice the preview popup by itself.

edits.find:
// Called from mouseenter handlers: a tap would leave it up for good.
        if (_isTouchCompatMouseEvent()) return;

name: the per-image type tooltip shows on a tap again
why: Removes the guard from _showLiTooltip() only; the preview popup keeps its own.

name: sticky page headers start on a touch device again
why: Drops the touch gate from _stickyPageHeadersWanted(): the feature initialises on a phone without the opt-in.

name: bars are clamped to clientWidth on a touch device again
why: The pre-fix width: _sphViewportWidth() returns clientWidth everywhere, so on a zoomed-out phone every bar is squeezed (org/mobile.org bug 2, Image #11).

name: the desktop viewport width uses innerWidth too
why: Desktop must stay on clientWidth: with a classic scrollbar innerWidth includes it, so bars would end under it. KNOWN BLIND SPOT, hence expect pass: headless Chromium has overlay scrollbars, so innerWidth == clientWidth there (probe-mobile-sph.js desktop arm, 2026-10-03: 1280 / 1280) and the desktop spec's overhang assertion cannot see the difference. Only a headed browser with a classic scrollbar could.
grep: pins header, entity header, tabs, h2 bars and footer
